newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Foster's wine unit moves into U.S., Chile.
newsitem.headline: Foster's wine unit moves into U.S., Chile.

text.p: Mildara Blass, the wine division of Foster's Brewing Group, said on Tuesday it had begun its overseas production thrust, setting up a joint venture in Chile and winemaking operations in the United States.

Mildara chief executive Ray King told Reuters he expected the two ventures to produce up to A$30 million annual revenue within four or five years of establishment and that Mildara would seek to further expand international production. "Our first venture is the U.S. and Chile, we will obviously look at Argentina and, if things progress reasonably well, then we will start to look elsewhere and that will be in Europe," he said.

King said Mildara had set up a joint venture to produce and market a jointly-owned new global wine brand, aimed primarily at the U.S. and United Kingdom markets, with one of Chile's leading wine companies, Vina Santa Carolina.

The Chilean company would provide facilities and resources, earning production profits from the venture, while Mildara would contribute winemaking expertise and working capital and would earn distribution profits, he said.

"While the profit margins will not be quite as good as our existing profit margins, the investment initially will be very low so the actual return on investment will be very high," he said, adding the joint venture had already begun operations.

Santa Carolina's annual production volume was similar to Mildara, which crushed about 47,000 tonnes of premium grapes in the 1997 vintage, and the joint venture was expected to have annual revenue of about A$15 million within five years, he said.
King said Vina Santa Carolina also had a major investment in the large and lucrative Argentinian market which was expected to form the basis for a further joint venture with Mildara.

In setting up its United States' winemaking venture, he said Mildara had entered into contracts to buy grapes and use winery facilities in California from the October 1997 vintage, with targeted annual revenue similar to the Chilean joint venture.
"Seventy percent of the U.S. market is satisfied out of California, whereas about two percent of US demand is satisfied from Australia," King said of Mildara's strategy.
"We would like to fish in a bigger ocean," he said.
